key_findings.title: Monocular Depth Estimation: A Survey
key_findings.summary: Comprehensive review of traditional and deep‑learning approaches up to 2023. Covers supervised, self‑supervised and semi‑supervised paradigms, benchmark datasets (KITTI, NYU‑Depth, Make3D, etc.), evaluation metrics, and discusses open challenges such as domain shift, handling non‑Lambertian surfaces and real‑time deployment.

key_findings.title: SPIdepth: Strengthened Pose Information for Self‑Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
key_findings.summary: Introduces a larger, pretrained PoseNet to stabilize motion estimation in self‑supervised training. Achieves state‑of‑the‑art results on KITTI (AbsRel 0.029) and wins the NTIRE 2025 HR Mono Depth Challenge, demonstrating improved robustness on transparent and mirror surfaces.

key_findings.title: SoccerNet 2025 Challenges Results – Monocular Depth Estimation Track
key_findings.summary: Provides a large‑scale, sport‑broadcast benchmark for relative depth from single‑camera video. Highlights the gap between academic benchmarks (KITTI, NYU) and real‑world broadcast data, and shows that transformer‑based architectures with multi‑scale attention achieve the best scores.

key_findings.title: Multi‑task learning with cross‑task consistency for improved depth estimation in colonoscopy
key_findings.summary: Applies monocular depth estimation to medical endoscopy. Uses a shared encoder with surface‑normal and depth decoders plus a cross‑task consistency loss, yielding ~15 % relative error reduction over the BTS baseline on the C3VD dataset. Shows the benefit of auxiliary geometric tasks in low‑texture domains.

key_findings.title: A Survey on Deep 3D Human Pose Estimation
key_findings.summary: Although focused on pose, this 2024 survey dedicates a substantial section to depth‑ambiguity solutions in monocular setups, including depth‑aware pose lifting and diffusion models. It is frequently cited by recent depth‑estimation works for its analysis of geometric priors.

synthesis: The period 2023‑2025 has witnessed rapid convergence of three trends in monocular depth estimation. First, self‑supervised learning has become the dominant paradigm, moving away from expensive dense LiDAR supervision. Works such as SPIdepth demonstrate that the often‑overlooked pose estimation component is a critical bottleneck; strengthening it with pretrained representations yields large gains and improves robustness on challenging surfaces (transparent, reflective). Second, the community is expanding the domain of application. Beyond autonomous‑driving benchmarks (KITTI, Cityscapes), new challenges like SoccerNet 2025 and medical colonoscopy introduce diverse lighting, motion, and texture conditions, exposing the limits of existing models and spurring multi‑task and transformer‑based designs. Third, survey literature has matured, with the 2023 "Monocular Depth Estimation: A Survey" providing a solid taxonomy of supervised/self‑supervised methods and outlining open problems (domain adaptation, real‑time inference, uncertainty). The 2024 pose‑estimation survey further contextualizes depth ambiguity solutions, encouraging cross‑disciplinary ideas such as diffusion priors and large‑language‑model‑derived semantic cues. Collectively, these developments point to a future where monocular depth estimation will be (a) more physically grounded through better pose and surface normal supervision, (b) more generalizable across domains via multi‑task consistency and large‑scale pretraining, and (c) evaluated on increasingly realistic, task‑specific benchmarks.
